policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, scene_frame, first_cross_t; the crossing that brings crossings to N-1 often happens inside the frames of the very step where the decision is made), then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values and the cube motion in this step's frames: - Predict the timing. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so first_cross_t is a quarter period and the Nth arrival at the target is predicted at T_N = (2N-1)*first_cross_t. Compute remaining = T_N - (timestep of the scene at this decision step). While first_cross_t is empty, crossings is 0 and no timing is needed. - Determine the cube's direction from the last two frames shown at this step, using their timesteps: v = (cube_x at the last frame - cube_x at the previous frame) / (last timestep - previous timestep). Always divide by the time gap. Take the cube's side at the last frame (smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, larger_x if cube_x > target_x). The cube is HEADING BACK toward the target if it is on the larger_x side and v < 0, or on the smaller_x side and v > 0, or its cube_x is identical in the last two frames (fully stopped at the turnaround). Otherwise it is RUNNING OUT (moving away from the target on its current side); this includes the case where the two frames lie on different sides, since the cube has just crossed. Do not treat a small |v| as the turnaround: cube speed varies by a factor of three across episodes, and a slow cube that has just crossed is still far from returning. Do not use |cube_x - target_x| shrinking or growing as the test: it shrinks across a crossing even though the cube is then moving away. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND any of: (a) remaining <= 30 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land); (b) the timestep of the scene at this decision step is at or past the predicted turnaround (2N-2)*first_cross_t, with no slack (equivalently remaining <= first_cross_t); (c) the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above. No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is RUNNING OUT by the test above with remaining > 30 and the scene timestep still before the predicted turnaround (2N-2)*first_cross_t (including the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding, and while it is still on its way out to the far end, even when only a few timesteps short of the turnaround). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above or remaining <= 30, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the side of the carried-in scene_frame (smaller_x if its cube_x < its target_x, else larger_x; skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2

fields.name: first_cross_t
fields.description: Carry it unchanged if it is already set. If it is empty and the crossings count you just computed at this step is 1 or more, find the first consecutive pair in this step's side sequence whose side differs; the earlier member is either the carried-in scene_frame or a frame of this step, the later member is a frame of this step. With t1, t2 their timesteps, d1 = cube_x - target_x at the earlier frame (its own target_x) and d2 likewise at the later frame, write t1 + (t2 - t1) * |d1| / (|d1| + |d2|), rounded half up to a whole timestep. Never extrapolate; the carried-in scene_frame always supplies the frame before a flip that precedes this step's first frame. Otherwise leave it empty. e.g. 30

fields.name: scene_frame
fields.description: Write the ordered list [timestep, cube_x, target_x] of the scene at this decision step (the last frame shown). Overwrite it every step; at the first step it is the t=0 frame. The side of the target line for any frame is smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, else larger_x; the carried-in scene_frame gives the side, timestep and positions of the last frame of the previous step, and is the frame before the flip whenever a crossing lies between the previous scene and this step's first frame. e.g. [56, 104, 117]
